questions.question: What input does a cross-encoder score?
options: A pair of independently computed vectors compared by cosine
A pooled document vector paired with the query's BM25 score
A single sequence holding the query and the document together
A document vector compared against a query-side lexical index

questions.question: Why can a cross-encoder not precompute document representations offline?
options: Its document embeddings expire whenever the index is rebuilt
Its document tokens are re-encoded while attending to the query
Its scoring head provides no document-side input layer at all
Its precomputed logits cannot be held in an approximate index

questions.question: A cross-encoder scores pairs in batches of 32 at about 18 ms per batch. Rescoring 100 candidates costs roughly how much model time?
options: About 18 ms
About 36 ms
About 40 ms
About 72 ms

questions.question: A query asks for stretching routines that do not load the knee. Why does a cross-encoder handle this better than lexical or single-vector matching?
options: It binds the negation to the constrained phrase in joint attention
It drops negation words before scoring so the phrase matches cleanly
It expands the query with synonyms for low-impact knee exercises
It scores only documents whose text contains no negation at all

questions.question: A reranker truncates every document at 512 tokens. After the retrieval stage switches to focused passages, reranked quality rises. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Shorter inputs let the model attend over a wider batch dimension
Passage retrieval shrinks the vocabulary the encoder must cover
The decisive evidence now sits inside the scored token window
Shorter passages raise the term overlap the scorer can reward

questions.question: A team blends raw cross-encoder logits with BM25 scores and the merged ordering becomes erratic. What is the underlying defect?
options: BM25 scores cannot be computed for passages shorter than a page
Uncalibrated logits and BM25 scores live on incomparable scales
The reranker was trained with too few transformer layers to blend
Logits and term scores sort in opposite directions by convention

questions.topic: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
questions.question: What does a bi-encoder precompute for retrieval?
options: One joint encoding for every likely query and document pair
A full attention map between every query and document token
One relevance logit per document for each class of query
One fixed-size vector per document, built offline at ingest

questions.topic: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
questions.question: Why is bi-encoder retrieval so cheap per query?
options: It avoids tokenizing the document text at any point in the pipeline
It swaps the transformer encoder for a much smaller linear model
Documents are encoded once, so only the query is encoded online
It caches the answer for every query the index has already seen

questions.topic: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
questions.question: Which query is most likely to expose a bi-encoder's weakness relative to a cross-encoder?
options: Find the datasheet for part ZX-4817-Q rev 3
What are common treatments for lower back pain
How do I improve battery life on my phone
Show me recent articles about electric vehicles

questions.topic: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
questions.question: A service searches 5 million passages at 300 queries per second with an 80 ms reranking budget. Which architecture fits?
options: Cross-encoder scoring of every passage in the corpus per query
Bi-encoder retrieval with a cross-encoder over a shortlist
Cross-encoder scoring of 5,000 candidates for each query served
BM25 alone, with no learned model anywhere in the serving path

questions.topic: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
questions.question: A team tries replacing its bi-encoder retriever with a cross-encoder over the full corpus and abandons the plan. What blocked them?
options: Cross-encoders cannot accept documents longer than 512 tokens
Cross-encoders need graded relevance labels at serving time
One forward pass per pair makes corpus-wide scoring far too slow
Cross-encoders cannot share one accelerator across replicas

questions.topic: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
questions.question: Which system can most reasonably skip the bi-encoder stage entirely?
options: A public web engine indexing ten million crawled pages
A news service answering five thousand queries per second
A multilingual archive rebuilt from scratch every night
A 4,000-document policy search with modest query traffic

questions.topic: Rerank Depth: How Many Candidates to Rescore
questions.question: What does rerank depth mean?
options: How many first-stage candidates the reranker actually rescores
How many transformer layers the reranking model stacks
How many tokens of each candidate passage the model reads
How many retrieval sources contribute to the fused list

questions.topic: Rerank Depth: How Many Candidates to Rescore
questions.question: What is the main risk of setting rerank depth too shallow?
options: The reranker drifts away from its training distribution
Relevant candidates below the cutoff are never rescued
The retrieval index doubles in storage as depth is trimmed
Candidate scores lose their order within the fused list

questions.topic: Rerank Depth: How Many Candidates to Rescore
questions.question: In a depth sweep, which property identifies the right operating point on the curve?
options: The point where candidate recall first reaches exactly 1.0
The point where total system latency reaches its minimum
The knee where added quality flattens against added latency
The point where the reranker sees every retrieved candidate

questions.topic: Rerank Depth: How Many Candidates to Rescore
questions.question: At 200 queries per second and a rerank depth of 100, how many pair evaluations per second must the reranking fleet sustain?
options: 20,000 pairs per second
2,000 pairs per second
200,000 pairs per second
200 pairs per second

questions.topic: Rerank Depth: How Many Candidates to Rescore
questions.question: After depth doubles from 100 to 200, offline quality rises slightly but production quality falls during traffic peaks. What most likely happened?
options: The retriever stopped returning enough candidates to fill depth
The reranker lost access to the labels it calibrates against
Deduplication collapsed the relevant documents at peak volume
Batch timeouts fired and the fallback served retrieval order

questions.topic: Rerank Depth: How Many Candidates to Rescore
questions.question: A retriever upgrade moves relevant documents from rank 150 toward rank 40. What happens to the optimal rerank depth?
options: It must rise, because candidate recall now depends on depth
It can usually fall, since the same quality needs fewer pairs
It stops depending on the latency budget the service allows
It must be reset to match the new embedding dimension exactly
